sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Very interesting! When clicking one at a time:
- Click 1 (50,30): (50,30) → N, others gray
- Click 2 (55,25): (55,25) → N, (50,30) stays N
- Click 3 (55,35): (55,35) → N, (50,30) and (55,25) stay N
- Click 4 (60,30): ALL blocks revert to gray!
So the pattern is: clicking the 4th cross-position block causes ALL to revert to gray. This is like a "reset" trigger!
This means I can have at most 3 of the 4 cross blocks be green (N) at the same time. Clicking the 4th one resets everything.
So the goal might be to have exactly 3 of the 4 cross blocks green, matching some pattern. Or maybe the goal involves the bar, not the grid.
Let me think about the left grid pattern again. It has 4 purple dots in a cross. But maybe the goal isn't to match that pattern exactly. Maybe the left grid is just a reference or decoration.
Let me reconsider the bar. The bar has a blue head on the left, a gray body, and blue/sky-blue tips on the right. When I press RIGHT, the bar extends. When I press LEFT, it shrinks. Maybe the goal involves the bar reaching a certain position.
Or maybe the goal involves clicking the bar itself, or clicking the purple dots in the left grid.
Let me try a completely different approach: click on the purple dots in the left grid to see what happens.
